$comment: The architecture, in the only form that stays true: something CI can fail on.
ARCHITECTURE.md explains the reasoning; this file is what is enforced.
Every workspace package is a module with one owner, one public entry point,
and a tier. A module may only depend on modules of a strictly lower tier.

tiers.name: kernel
tiers.purpose: Shared contracts and pure helpers. Depends on nothing.

tiers.name: telemetry
tiers.purpose: Structured logging and metrics, needed by everything below the apps.

tiers.name: platform
tiers.purpose: Cross-cutting infrastructure primitives with no business meaning.

tiers.name: persistence
tiers.purpose: The database and the repository interfaces over it.

tiers.name: protocol
tiers.purpose: Adapters that speak OAuth and MCP to the outside world.

tiers.name: capability
tiers.purpose: The gateway's business capability: federation, policy, catalogue.

tiers.name: composition
tiers.purpose: Wires the modules together and owns the HTTP surface.

tiers.name: entrypoint
tiers.purpose: The deployables. No library may depend on these.

tiers.name: harness
tiers.purpose: Mock upstreams and fixtures that stand a whole gateway up for a test.

tiers.name: suite
tiers.purpose: The conformance suite, which exercises the deployables through the harness.

$comment: The shared kernel is the one module everything imports, so it is the one
module that must not grow a dependency. It may use pure Node builtins and
nothing else: an import of a driver, a socket or the filesystem here would
put infrastructure underneath every business rule in the repository.
Names that attract unrelated code and become the file every branch edits.
A file should be named for what it is. If nothing fits, the code probably
belongs in the module that uses it.
